players.product: copper-clad laminate (CCL), thin-core and prepreg for package substrates and AI-server PCBs (Electro-Materials BG, 'Doosan Electronics')

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, filed 08-14-2026): the Electro-Materials BG, the copper-clad-laminate business, generated segment revenue of KRW 1,293,352M against KRW 879,071M in the year-earlier half, roughly 47% growth, and segment operating profit of KRW 386,913M against KRW 252,313M, a margin near 30%. On 12.1% of group revenue the unit produced 43.2% of group operating profit. Segment net profit was KRW 317,353M and segment assets rose to KRW 1,948,103M from KRW 1,398,847M at the end of 2025. External CCL revenue was KRW 1,293,293M, split KRW 858,904M export and KRW 434,389M domestic; by region the unit billed KRW 859,057M into Asia and KRW 438,836M domestically. The company describes its CCL as a core material for AI accelerators, semiconductors, communications equipment and smartphones, with the main products being NetworkBoard (NWB) CCL for AI accelerators and data centers, package (PKG) CCL for semiconductors, halogen-free CCL for optical modules and flexible CCL for smartphones.
quarterly_data.figure: Electro-Materials segment H1 revenue KRW 1,293,352M vs KRW 879,071M; segment operating profit KRW 386,913M vs KRW 252,313M; 43.21% of group operating profit on 12.09% of group revenue; segment assets KRW 1,948,103M vs KRW 1,398,847M

quarterly_data.signal: Group financials: H1 2026 consolidated revenue KRW 10,617,501M against KRW 9,617,666M a year earlier, operating profit KRW 830,730M against KRW 552,857M, half-year net profit KRW 637,116M against KRW 244,460M. Q2 alone: revenue KRW 5,586,147M and operating profit KRW 488,426M. On a parent-only basis, which is essentially the Electro-Materials and Digital Innovation businesses plus the holding company, operating revenue was KRW 1,132,000M against KRW 839,876M and operating profit KRW 266,819M against KRW 176,887M. The consolidated debt-to-equity ratio fell to 161.30% from 169.14%.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 consolidated revenue KRW 10,617,501M (prior half KRW 9,617,666M); operating profit KRW 830,730M (prior half KRW 552,857M); Q2 revenue KRW 5,586,147M / operating profit KRW 488,426M; parent-only operating profit KRW 266,819M

quarterly_data.signal: CCL capacity and utilisation (section II-3): H1 2026 nameplate capacity and output in thousands of units were 3,191 and 2,435 at Iksan and Gimje for 76.3% utilisation, 2,220 and 2,437 at Jeungpyeong for 109.8%, 2,016 and 2,071 at Gimcheon for 102.7% and 3,156 and 2,911 in China for 92.2%. Two of the three Korean laminate lines ran above nameplate through the half. Segment inventory built to KRW 521,924M from KRW 359,978M at the end of 2025, with raw materials and stores at KRW 315,898M against KRW 209,200M, on a pull from AI data-center and semiconductor demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Jeungpyeong utilisation 109.8% and Gimcheon 102.7% (above nameplate); Iksan/Gimje 76.3%, China 92.2%; segment inventory KRW 521,924M vs KRW 359,978M, raw materials KRW 315,898M vs KRW 209,200M

quarterly_data.signal: CCL capacity investment: KRW 88,085M was spent on CCL machinery in H1 2026 after KRW 89,663M in 2025 and KRW 38,699M in 2024. The forward plan commits KRW 755,135M to CCL equipment, of which KRW 299,531M falls in 2026, KRW 287,030M in 2027 and KRW 168,575M in 2028; including the electrical-materials and flexible lines and IT infrastructure the total planned programme is KRW 824,188M. A new overseas laminate plant is being added: Doosan Electro-Materials (Thailand) Co., Ltd. was incorporated on 04-27-2026 and is held 99.99% through the Singapore holding company; the 03-31-2026 board approved a capital increase into Doosan Electro-Materials Singapore of KRW 29,510M and a payment guarantee for the Thai company, and the parent has since guaranteed USD 110,000 thousand of facility funding from the Export-Import Bank of Korea running June 2026 to June 2031 at 4.78%. The Vietnamese laminate plant continues to draw parent loans totalling USD 24,500 thousand at 4.60%.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 CCL capex KRW 88,085M; planned CCL programme KRW 755,135M (KRW 299,531M in 2026, KRW 287,030M in 2027, KRW 168,575M in 2028); Thailand plant guaranteed USD 110,000 thousand of Eximbank facility funding; KRW 29,510M capital increase into the Singapore holding company

quarterly_data.signal: CCL pricing and input costs: the average laminate selling price rose to KRW 69,132 per unit in H1 2026 from KRW 60,127 in 2025 and KRW 51,022 in 2024, which the company attributes to a richer product mix and higher raw-material prices. Raw-material purchases for the segment were KRW 502,596M. Copper foil cost KRW 32,063 per kilogram against KRW 23,821 in 2025 and KRW 20,943 in 2024, glass fabric KRW 6,967 per metre against KRW 5,196 and KRW 4,094, and epoxy resin KRW 12,655 per kilogram against KRW 10,774 and KRW 9,869; the filing attributes the increases to rising demand. Named suppliers, all non-affiliates, are Circuit Foil, Co-Tech and Mitsui Mining and Smelting for copper foil; Nitto Boseki, Taiwan Glass Industry and Asahi Kasei for glass fabric; Kukdo Chemical, Kolon Industries and Nippon Kayaku for epoxy resin; and Kaneka, Pharmicell and Admatechs for films and chemicals. Copper foil tracks the LME price and glass fabric tracks yarn.
quarterly_data.figure: CCL average price KRW 69,132 per unit vs KRW 60,127 (2025) and KRW 51,022 (2024); copper foil KRW 32,063/kg vs KRW 23,821; glass fabric KRW 6,967/m vs KRW 5,196; epoxy resin KRW 12,655/kg vs KRW 10,774; segment raw-material purchases KRW 502,596M
quarterly_data.counterparty: Circuit Foil; Co-Tech; Mitsui Mining & Smelting; Nitto Boseki; Taiwan Glass Industry; Asahi Kasei; Kukdo Chemical; Kolon Industries; Nippon Kayaku; Kaneka; Pharmicell; Admatechs

quarterly_data.signal: Market position and mix shift: the company estimates its Q2 2026 global CCL share at 30% in package CCL, 22% in flexible CCL (single and double sided) and 16% in halogen-free CCL. The sales strategy has moved away from commodity grades toward high-function products, specifically NWB CCL for AI accelerators and data centers, PKG CCL for semiconductors and halogen-free CCL for optical modules, sold into the global market, and 2026 targets a higher weighting of high-value products together with supply diversification to global customers beyond Samsung. The unit says CCL requires prior quality and specification approval from both the set maker and the PCB maker before it can be used, and that the industry is led by roughly ten suppliers from Korea, China, Taiwan and Japan.
quarterly_data.figure: Estimated global share Q2 2026: package CCL 30%, flexible CCL 22%, halogen-free CCL 16%

quarterly_data.signal: Research pipeline aimed at the next accelerator generation: the 2026 project list includes a Highly Advanced Low Loss laminate for next-generation AI accelerators, an environmentally friendly extreme-low-Df material intended to pre-empt the low-dielectric CCL market; a low-CTE fluorine-based CCL for rigid backplanes to enter the fluoropolymer high-layer-count market; a high-reliability low-stretch flexible CCL for displays; a low-dielectric flexible CCL for foldable and flagship phones; a low-power 28GHz 5G millimetre-wave antenna module; and a non-memory die-attach-film product for semiconductor packages aimed at mid-size OSAT customers in Greater China. Group research spending was KRW 256,386M in the half, 2.41% of revenue, across 353 projects. The Electro-Materials unit holds 137 domestic and 91 overseas patents and utility models.
quarterly_data.figure: Group R&D KRW 256,386M, 2.41% of revenue, 353 projects; Electro-Materials holds 137 domestic and 91 overseas patents

quarterly_data.signal: Post-period-end acquisition of a wafer maker: on 07-31-2026 the board approved and the company signed a share purchase agreement to acquire 70.61% of SK Siltron from SK Corporation, described as securing a mid-to-long-term growth base through business diversification. The deposit was paid immediately after signing but the conditions precedent and closing were not complete at the reporting date, so SK Siltron is not consolidated and no business combination is recognised in the half-year statements. The war chest came largely from the sale of 11,700,000 Doosan Robotics shares at KRW 81,000 each, completed on 02-27-2026 for KRW 947,700M and booked as a KRW 923,040M disposal gain, which is why parent-only net profit reached KRW 971,894M in the half.
quarterly_data.figure: Share purchase agreement for 70.61% of SK Siltron signed 07-31-2026, not yet closed; funded partly by the KRW 947,700M sale of 11,700,000 Doosan Robotics shares at KRW 81,000 (KRW 923,040M gain)

quarterly_data.signal: Corporate value-up plan disclosed 04-01-2026 commits to mid-to-long-term expansion of the electronics division's production capacity and to new overseas production subsidiaries as the growth base, to a portfolio strengthened around advanced materials and semiconductors, and to shareholder returns comprising a payout ratio of at least 25% with total dividends at least 10% above the prior year, plus cancellation within 2026 of all treasury shares other than the 632,500 common shares retained for employee restricted-stock awards. Quarterly dividends began in Q1 2026 at KRW 1,000 per share, repeated in Q2, and 330,000 treasury shares were already cancelled on 11-17-2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Value-up plan: electronics capacity expansion plus new overseas plants; payout ratio 25% or more and dividends up 10% or more; treasury shares beyond 632,500 to be cancelled in 2026; quarterly dividend KRW 1,000 per share

quarterly_data.signal: Group order backlog at 06-30-2026 was KRW 29,518,741M, or KRW 29,276,720M after removing the discontinued logistics unit, against KRW 25,340,901M at the start of the year. Doosan Enerbility holds KRW 27,040,162M of that, led by the Czech Dukovany 5 and 6 nuclear steam supply system contract with Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power, worth KRW 5,063,505M, signed 12-15-2025, running to 04-18-2038 and only 6.43% complete; Doosan Fuel Cell holds KRW 1,930,238M. The energy unit had booked 24 large gas turbines in total by the half-year end, 12 of them in 2026 alone (5 domestic and 7 overseas), for more than 10.7GW of supplied capacity, and won the Oman Duqm 870MW combined-cycle plant in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: Group order backlog KRW 29,518,741M at 06-30-2026 (KRW 25,340,901M at the start of the year); Doosan Enerbility KRW 27,040,162M including the KRW 5,063,505M Czech Dukovany NSSS contract; 24 large gas turbines contracted for over 10.7GW

quarterly_data.signal: Power demand from AI is the stated driver across the group's energy businesses. The filing cites the IEA forecast that electricity demand grew 3.0% in 2025 and will average 3.6% a year from 2026 to 2030 on electrification and large data-center construction, and notes that 2025 gas combined-cycle orders rose 41% year on year to 96GW and that gas combined cycle will keep expanding to cover data-center load. The fuel-cell unit says surging data-center power demand is creating grid bottlenecks and pushing buyers toward behind-the-meter distributed generation, for which modular fuel cells that can be installed quickly and scaled with each data-center phase are presented as the practical solution, with the largest opportunity in exports to United States data centers; cumulative Korean fuel-cell installations reached 1,477MW at 06-30-2026 of which Doosan supplied 731MW, about 50%.
quarterly_data.figure: IEA electricity demand +3.0% in 2025 and +3.6% a year 2026-2030; 2025 gas combined-cycle orders +41% to 96GW; Korean cumulative fuel-cell installations 1,477MW with Doosan at 731MW (about 50%)

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor-adjacent subsidiaries and stakes: Doosan Tesna, the system-semiconductor test house, turned to profit with H1 revenue of KRW 157,755M and net profit of KRW 15,486M against KRW 135,197M and a KRW 16,943M net loss a year earlier, running wafer test at 57.8% utilisation, package test at 58.2% and die preparation at 8.9%. The Chinese laminate arms grew hard: Doosan Shanghai Chemical Materials posted H1 revenue of KRW 501,083M and Doosan Electro-Materials (Changshu) KRW 334,744M with net profit of KRW 36,920M, against KRW 182,147M and KRW 19,045M a year earlier; parent sales of laminate into the Shanghai unit were KRW 451,507M and into the Singapore unit KRW 66,917M in the half. The company also holds 3.90% of the Korean design house SEMIFIVE at KRW 20,359M and took a new 19% interest in Alpha AI Architecture Fund L.P. for KRW 6,680M during the half.
quarterly_data.figure: Doosan Tesna H1 revenue KRW 157,755M / net profit KRW 15,486M (prior half KRW 135,197M / KRW 16,943M loss); Changshu laminate revenue KRW 334,744M vs KRW 182,147M; SEMIFIVE stake 3.90% at KRW 20,359M; new 19% stake in Alpha AI Architecture Fund for KRW 6,680M
